entries.claim: A tunnel carries one protocol inside another, so a reachability that policy forbids directly can be reintroduced through a host both sides accept — the boundary that matters is the tunnel endpoint, not the inner protocol.
steps: Prove the sink reads a file at all BEFORE testing traversal: fetch a file you KNOW exists on the target and confirm real content comes back.
If you cannot get a known-good read, there is no traversal finding to report — the sink is not proven.
Then apply the traversal value and confirm the returned content is from OUTSIDE the intended directory. Content, not status code.
Reject any result where only the status line differs: proxies, error handlers and WAFs produce status differentials with no file ever read.

entries.claim: A pivot is established by tunnelling traffic for a second network segment through the already-compromised host, which carries no credentials of its own.
steps: Identify the check and the use as TWO separate operations, and measure the gap between them.
Fire many parallel attempts (tens to hundreds) so at least one lands inside the window.
Vary ONLY the timing; the payload and session stay fixed.
Report a rate, not a single success: N successes in M attempts both proves the window and tells the reader whether it is practical to exploit.
